ticket.title: Fifteen fields still disagree across Rust and TypeScript, in three entities that each need a decision
ticket.description:
PROGRESS 2026-10-30. From 9 entities / 33 fields: the comparator fixes (GB-239) removed the nesting false positives and the declared secret, class A mirrored 3 fields (4857c03: task_edge, task_node now clean) and 1eaec01 mirrored AnonymizedSynthesisTrace properly - verification/task_key/head_commit_sha plus VerificationReport and CompilerDiagnostic interfaces, since two of those are nested structs rather than fields. Measured 18 -> 15, and that entity drops out of the report.

REMAINING 15 lines in 3 entities, and all three need a decision rather than a copy:

chat_message (7) - Rust content/timestamp_ms/token_count versus TypeScript text/timestamp/latency_ms/model_used. Rust is the persisted shape in .gaugeblock/chat/threads.jsonl; TypeScript is render state. Options: rename the UI fields, add a mapper at the fetch boundary (recommended - text/latencyMs/modelUsed are display concerns a rename would drag into the wire format), or declare genuinely different types and stop matching the names.

dado_pattern (3) - canonical_example_fills and required_imports exist only in Rust, `domain` only in TypeScript. Stale in both directions, so one side must gain and the other must lose.

typed_hole (5) - ast_node_kind (Rust) versus kind (TypeScript) is a rename of one field, not two drifts; max_tokens and allow_literals are Rust-only; description is TypeScript-only. Deciding the canonical spelling settles three of the five.
acceptance_criteria: Mirror anonymized_synthesis_trace including a VerificationReport interface, then re-measure
Decide chat_message: rename, mapper, or distinct types - with the decision recorded, since the Rust side is persisted data and the TS side is render state
Resolve dado_pattern in both directions and typed_hole (rename plus the two missing fields)
miter contracts --check passes with only the declared api_key exception

completed_items: Criterion 1 met: all 9 entities classified against the actual sources, not the report. TypeScript sides are all in benchwork/web/src and the file header declares them wire contracts, so the comparison is legitimate rather than a name collision. 33 lines reconcile exactly into: 5 stale-mirror fields (add to TS, Rust canonical), 16 diverged fields needing a canonical-spelling decision (chat_message, typed_hole, dado_pattern), 11 structural false positives (docs_config, workspace_capabilities - nesting, not drift), 1 deliberate security asymmetry (role_override_config.api_key must stay Rust-only). Criterion 3 filed as GB-239 with the two comparator defects and the reduction from 33 to 21 lines it should produce.
remaining_items: Criterion 2, in two separable pieces. (a) The 5 stale-mirror fields are mechanical but need a TypeScript toolchain check: adding a required field to an interface breaks every object literal that constructs it, so each addition has to be followed by tsc over benchwork/web. (b) The 16 diverged fields need a decision per entity before any rename: chat_message has content vs text and timestamp_ms vs timestamp, where the Rust side is the persisted ledger shape and the TS side is what the UI renders, so aligning may mean a mapper rather than a rename.
handoff.last_error_or_blocker: None. Note that the gate is red on contracts until GB-239 lands: 12 of the 33 lines cannot be satisfied by any code change, so criterion 2 alone cannot turn it green.

completed_items: Class A partly done and measured: 4857c03 mirrored TaskEdge.target_ticket_key, TaskEdge.target_repo and TaskNode.archived_at_epoch_ms into benchwork/web, tsc --noEmit clean, and miter contracts went 20 -> 18 with task_edge and task_node dropping out of the report entirely. Corrected the filing: anonymized_synthesis_trace is NOT mechanical - its verification field is a nested VerificationReport struct, so it needs a second interface plus its diagnostics child.
remaining_items: 18 lines in 4 entities. anonymized_synthesis_trace: 2 trivial Option<String> fields plus the nested VerificationReport mirror. chat_message: the decision case - Rust is the persisted ledger shape, TypeScript is render state, so rename vs mapper vs distinct types. dado_pattern: stale in both directions. typed_hole: ast_node_kind vs kind is a rename, plus two Rust-only and one TypeScript-only field.
handoff.last_error_or_blocker: None. Every remaining line is real drift; the gate cannot go green until these 18 are resolved or declared, and declaring them would be wrong - none is a secret or a nesting artifact.

completed_items: anonymized_synthesis_trace mirrored in 1eaec01 with its nested VerificationReport and CompilerDiagnostic interfaces; measured 18 -> 15 drift lines and the entity drops out. Verified entities rose 35 -> 37 because the two new interfaces are themselves cross-referenced. tsc --noEmit clean.
remaining_items: 15 lines in 3 entities, each blocked on a decision rather than on effort: chat_message needs rename-vs-mapper-vs-distinct-types (recommend mapper, since Rust is persisted and TS is render state); dado_pattern is stale in both directions so one side gains and one loses; typed_hole needs a canonical spelling for ast_node_kind vs kind, which settles three of its five lines.
handoff.last_error_or_blocker: Owner decision on the three, specifically chat_message: a rename pushes UI vocabulary into the persisted wire format, a mapper keeps them separate at the cost of a translation layer.

task.title: Nine entities drift across Rust and TypeScript: 32 fields disagree (miter contracts --check now fails on them)

events.description: Measured 2026-10-30 with miter contracts over the suite index: 35 verified multi-language entities, 9 with drift, 32 field-level disagreements. Entities: anonymized_synthesis_trace, chat_message, dado_pattern, docs_config, role_override_config, task_edge, task_node, typed_hole, workspace_capabilities. The first one checked by hand is real, not a parser artifact: benchwork-core ChatMessage has id/role/content/timestamp_ms/token_count while benchwork/web/src/chat/types.ts has id/role/text/timestamp/latencyMs/modelUsed, so the wire names themselves differ (content vs text, timestamp_ms vs timestamp). Two different things may be tangled here and they need separating before any code changes: pairs that are genuinely one wire contract drifted apart (should be aligned), and pairs that merely share a name across a Rust ledger record and a TypeScript UI state model (the checker matches by entity name, so those are false obligations).
acceptance_criteria: Classify all 9 entities as real wire drift or same-name-different-purpose, with the classification recorded
Align the real ones, deciding which side is canonical for each
Decide whether the checker should compare every same-named type or only entities declared as contracts, and make false obligations impossible rather than permanently allowlisted

events.title: Nine entities drift across Rust and TypeScript: 33 fields disagree (miter contracts --check fails on them)
events.description: Measured 2026-10-30 with miter contracts over a FRESH suite index: 35 verified multi-language entities, 9 with drift, 33 field-level disagreements. The ticket was filed as 32 fields and the difference is itself a finding: the index was three days stale when the count was taken, and after miter index . it grew to 33, i.e. the stale index was hiding a drift as well as symbols (GB-237). Entities: anonymized_synthesis_trace, chat_message, dado_pattern, docs_config, role_override_config, task_edge, task_node, typed_hole, workspace_capabilities. The one checked by hand is real, not a parser artifact: benchwork-core ChatMessage has id/role/content/timestamp_ms/token_count while benchwork/web/src/chat/types.ts has id/role/text/timestamp/latencyMs/modelUsed, so the wire names themselves differ (content vs text, timestamp_ms vs timestamp). Two things may be tangled and need separating before code changes: pairs that are genuinely one wire contract drifted apart, and pairs that merely share a name between a Rust ledger record and a TypeScript UI state model - the checker matches on entity name, so those are false obligations.

CLASSIFIED 2026-10-30. 9 entities / 33 fields, all TypeScript sides in benchwork/web/src, whose header declares them "wire contract interfaces matching benchwork-core" - so they are deliberate mirrors, not UI-local state, and the comparison is legitimate. The 9 split into four kinds, and the count reconciles exactly (2+1+2+7+5+4+9+2+1 = 33):

A. STALE MIRROR - Rust gained field(s), TS never followed. Add to TS, Rust canonical (5 fields). task_edge: target_repo, target_ticket_key. task_node: archived_at_epoch_ms. anonymized_synthesis_trace: task_key, verification.

B. DIVERGED - both sides changed, names differ; needs a per-entity decision on the canonical spelling (16 fields). chat_message: Rust content/timestamp_ms/token_count vs TS text/timestamp/latency_ms/model_used. typed_hole: Rust ast_node_kind/max_tokens/allow_literals vs TS kind/description - note ast_node_kind vs kind is a rename, not an omission. dado_pattern: Rust canonical_example_fills/required_imports vs TS domain.

C. STRUCTURAL FALSE POSITIVE - the checker compares top-level fields only, so a nested Rust struct inlined in TS reads as missing fields (11 fields). docs_config: Rust nests the nine doc entries under DocumentEntries while TS inlines them in DocsConfig.docs. workspace_capabilities: TS nests spec_docs { primary_spec_present, detected_files }, Rust mirrors that nesting, yet both fields are reported missing. These are not drift and must not be "fixed" by editing either side.

D. DELIBERATE ASYMMETRY - role_override_config.api_key exists in Rust and must NOT exist in TypeScript: it is a secret and the browser has no business receiving it (1 field). Adding it to satisfy the checker would be a security regression.

events.title: Eighteen fields still disagree across Rust and TypeScript, in four entities
events.description:
PROGRESS 2026-10-30. Original filing: 9 entities / 32-33 fields. After the comparator fixes (GB-239) the nesting false positives and the declared secret are gone, leaving 20 real lines; class A is now partly done (benchwork 4857c03 mirrored TaskEdge.target_ticket_key, TaskEdge.target_repo and TaskNode.archived_at_epoch_ms, measured 20 -> 18 with task_edge and task_node dropping out of the report entirely).

REMAINING 18 lines in 4 entities, none of them mechanical:

anonymized_synthesis_trace (3): head_commit_sha, task_key, verification. The first two are Option<String> and trivial; `verification` is a nested VerificationReport struct (ast_valid, typecheck_passed, tests_passed, duration_ms, diagnostics[], ...), so mirroring it means a second interface and its diagnostics child - which is why this entity is not class A after all.

chat_message (7): Rust content/timestamp_ms/token_count versus TypeScript text/timestamp/latency_ms/model_used. This is the decision case: Rust is the persisted ledger shape in .gaugeblock/chat/threads.jsonl, TypeScript is what the UI renders, and the honest options are (a) rename the UI fields, (b) add a mapper at the fetch boundary and let the UI keep its own vocabulary, or (c) declare them different types. Note the entity name matching is what pairs them at all.

dado_pattern (3): canonical_example_fills and required_imports exist only in Rust; `domain` exists only in TypeScript. Bidirectional, so at least one side is stale in both directions.

typed_hole (5): ast_node_kind versus `kind` is a rename, plus max_tokens and allow_literals missing from TypeScript and `description` missing from Rust.
acceptance_criteria: Mirror anonymized_synthesis_trace including a VerificationReport interface, then re-measure
Decide chat_message: rename, mapper, or distinct types - with the decision recorded, since the Rust side is persisted data and the TS side is render state
Resolve dado_pattern in both directions and typed_hole (rename plus the two missing fields)
miter contracts --check passes with only the declared api_key exception
